persona: Buyer for an online t-shirt shop

designs.title: Byron Bay
designs.why: Byron is a top-selling surf name and the lighthouse on the headland makes it read as the real place, not a stock beach. Engraving holds up full size, and the title and ring are clean on both tees. The side and top taglines are generic filler and vanish at chest size.
designs.fix: Drop or enlarge the tiny 'Ocean People Freedom' side text so the scene gets more room and the thumbnail reads cleaner.

designs.title: Playa Venao
designs.why: Well drawn and the signpost adds charm, but Playa Venao is a niche name with a small buyer pool. The scene is a generic palm-and-jungle cove, nothing that only Venao has, so it sells only to people who've been there.
designs.fix: Add one local marker (the wide crescent bay with Venao's headland, or a Panama hat/boat detail) so it feels specific rather than a template.

designs.title: Ericeira
designs.why: The strongest sense of place in the set: whitewashed clifftop town, stone walls, agave, a board leaning on the steps. It reads as Europe straight away and stands out on a page full of palm trees. Strong on the white main tee and solid on black.
designs.fix: Swap the generic 'Surf Tradition Ocean Spirit' for a real hook like 'World Surfing Reserve', which Ericeira fans actually wear with pride.

designs.title: San Juan del Sur
designs.why: The bay with the Christ statue on the hill is right and the 'Tacos / Amigos' signpost is fun. But 'Pura Vida' is Costa Rica's slogan, and Nicaraguan customers will call that out. The long name also crowds the arc, starting low on the left.
designs.fix: Replace 'Pura Vida' with a Nicaraguan line (e.g. 'Nica Libre' or 'Tranquilo') and tighten the title tracking so it sits evenly on the arc.

designs.title: Haleiwa
designs.why: North Shore is a great seller and the 'Shave Ice' sign is a nice local touch, but the mountain is clearly Diamond Head, which is in Honolulu on the south shore, not Haleiwa. Hawaii buyers will spot it at once and it makes the shirt look like a tourist knockoff.
designs.fix: Replace Diamond Head with the Waianae range / Mt Ka'ala and a North Shore reef break (or the Anahulu bridge), and use the okina in Hawai'i.

designs.title: Puerto Escondido
designs.why: Big name, and the heavy barreling wave fits Zicatela's 'Mexican Pipeline' reputation. 'Big Waves Wild Energy' is the one tagline in the set that sells. The long title is a bit cramped and lopsided on the left of the arc.
designs.fix: Rebalance the title arc so PUERTO and ESCONDIDO sit symmetrically around top center, and make the wave a bit bigger as the hero.

designs.title: Montañita
designs.why: The beach bar with signposts and string lights catches Montañita's party-surf vibe better than a plain beach, and the Ñ is handled correctly. The left half is busy and dark, so on the black tee it turns a bit muddy at a distance.
designs.fix: Open up the hut area (fewer leaves, more white space) so the left half doesn't clump at thumbnail and chest scale.

designs.title: Tamarindo
designs.why: Popular destination, and 'Pura Vida Siempre' is the right slogan here and sells. The wave rendering is the cleanest in the set. But the scene is the most generic of the eight: palm, beach, headland, sunset, nothing Tamarindo-specific.
designs.fix: Add a recognizable local cue such as Isla Capitán offshore or the estuary mouth to give it a reason to buy over any Costa Rica tee.
